title_fixed_en: How does the boat go up?

narration_estimate.status: unmeasured; replace with actual Piljae audio timings before production

hook.pattern: impossible-looking motion + reaction + one mechanism question
hook.line: 배가 물에 뜬 채 위층으로 올라갑니다. 처음 보면 기가 막히죠.
hook.emphasis: yellow reaction words within the normal caption size, short low hit; continuous gentle camera

clips.purpose: wide establishing view of the same single lock: boat approaches the open lower entrance; upper gate stays closed; chamber and lower canal levels match; only boat, wake and gentle camera move; same clean stylized look, colors and objects as the start frame; no added people, props or text
clips.start_frame: approved Blender wide approach frame; both lock ends and different canal levels visible
clips.end_frame: approved same-lock approach frame; gate geometry and water levels preserved

clips.purpose: boat exits through the already open upper gate at matched water levels; lower gate stays closed; smooth wide tracking; no gate or structure morphing; same clean stylized look, colors and objects as the start frame; no added people, props or text
clips.start_frame: approved Blender upper exit frame at equal chamber and upper canal level
clips.end_frame: approved wide boat exit frame with both lock ends in view

blender.camera_type: one main side cross-section view of the whole lock (lower canal left, chamber center, upper canal right; boat travels left to right) for at least 60 percent of runtime; a few slow medium shots that always return to it
groups: fixed lower canal (left) and upper canal (right) as simple channels
fixed lock chamber: floor and walls as clean blocks; near wall permanently cut away with a flat cut plane
lower gate pair and upper gate pair, simple mitre gates on hinge pivots
one upper inflow sluice and one lower outflow sluice as short visible channels in the cut plane, each with a small paddle that slides open
one boat: simple hull and cabin, the only orange object
chamber water: one surface that moves vertically, crisp level line visible in the cut plane
one person silhouette on the lockside for scale
model_detail: large clean shapes with small bevels; no repeated detail such as bolt rows, railings, ropes or ladders
subtle surface variation only (soft concrete tone, faint wood tone on gates) so materials read without clutter
water surface with gentle ripples and a small wake only while the boat moves
blender.materials: matte light-grey concrete, dark teal gates, orange boat, blue semi-transparent water; bright even light, soft shadows, AgX
blender.water_method: animated surface mesh, procedural normals, controlled water level and small wake; no large fluid simulation required

color_roles.gates: dark teal; yellow rim glow when named
color_roles.sluice_and_flow: blue arrows inside the cut plane
color_roles.water: clear blue with white level line

user_feedback: strong zooms hid the whole mechanism
phone safe areas made text at the very top hard to read
2026-10-11: tower crane 3D still not intuitive and too complex; simplify shapes, colors and camera

camera.rule: establish whole lock, explain from medium distance, return to whole lock after key actions; main objects stay readable

visual_direction.secondary_motion: small boat buoyancy motion, restrained wake, water ripples and gradual gate easing; no violent sloshing
visual_direction.layout_reference: config/higgsfield-typecast.json layout v4 (fixed title only, captions without panel)
visual_direction.texture_review: render style frames (hook, main side section, levels-equal moment, exit) at phone size; judge whether the moving part is obvious in 1 second, then material distinction

sound_design: original quiet canal ambience, low boat engine, gradual gate movement, inflow and outflow water; short low hit for the reveal; Piljae remains dominant
guards: upper and lower canal levels, chamber floor and walls remain fixed
boat floats at approximately constant draft and follows chamber water height; never rides a moving floor or lift
open entry or exit gates only after water levels on both sides match
never open both ends of the lock at once
close the lower outflow sluice before filling from the upper reach; close the upper inflow sluice before draining to the lower reach
do not animate water passing through closed solid gates, hulls or concrete; use the explicit sluice path
reverse-direction demonstration is identified as a separate example; do not teleport an exit boat back into the chamber
initial rise is a teaser; return to the entry with the spoken cue '먼저' and a short eased camera move back to the main view; no on-screen step text
show the full boat, both ends and water level relation during the main explanation
no abrupt punch-in; keep wide or medium shots for at least 80 percent of runtime
test the longest two-line caption and reaction phrase against conservative phone UI masks; never claim these coordinates are universal device safe areas
use generic single-chamber lock geometry; do not claim site dimensions, transit times or an operating procedure
measure final Piljae narration before committing shot times; do not trim speech
each generated source duration must cover its final timeline span; recheck total 50 seconds after timing changes
use shared layout v4: one fixed title y=500-660, captions y=1140-1380 without background, horizontal center x=540; no step chips or step headings
clarity before texture: no clutter props or repeated detail; the boat is the only orange object; one main side-section view keeps the same left-to-right orientation
show the level difference with the crisp water level lines on both sides of the closed gate, not with text
